2  JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.51,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Sri.Muruli, who met with road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief are that:
On 23-02-2024 at about 8-45 p.m. Muruli was proceeding as a pillion rider in a Honda Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LB-0847 from Mysore road towards Sumanahalli and when he reached near Sri Malai Mahadeshwara Temple, Nagarbhavi, Bangalore,
at that time the driver of Mini bus bearing No.KA-11-B-2969 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle, result of which, Muruli fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died at the spot.
So far, the petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards Transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequious ceremonies.
3. Prior to the accident, Muruli was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 40 years.
He was working at Private company and earning sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.

Due to the sudden death of Muruli,
petitioners have suffered mental agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. On service of notice, the Respondent no.1 appeared through his counsel but has not filed written statement and thereby uncontested the petition.

5. The respondent no.2/the insurer of Mini bus bearing No.KA-11-B-2969 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license and the said vehicle was not holding FC and permit and that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident.

It is further contended that the alleged accident has occurred on account of the negligent and careless act of Muruli and the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No KA-05-LB-0847 as rider was riding the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the motorcycle result of which Murali fell down on the road and Mini Bus going through the said road ran over Murali.

It is further contended that at the time of accident Murali was under the influence of alcohol and under the intoxication mind he did not sit properly on the vehicle result of which also he lost control and fell on the road and sustained head injuries.
It is further submitted that Muruli was not wearing helmet.
Hence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings following issues have been framed;
ISSUE 1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that, Muruli succumbed to the injuries sustained in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 23-02-2024 at about 8-45 pm., near Nagarbhavi ring road, near Venkatalakshmi vs Prathima N on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146720145/
3 Sri Malai Mahadeswara, Nagarbhavai, Bangalore, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA-11-B- 2969 ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the case, the 1 st petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P.10.
The respondent no.2 has examined its Administrative officer as RW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 to Ex.R3 and rider of the motorcycle by name Raju is examined as RW.2.

Preetham Shrikar -PSI at Jnana Bharathi Sanchari PS is examined as RW.3 and got marked documents as Ex.R4 to Ex.R8.
8.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent no.2 and perused the materials placed on record.

9. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- Petitioners have categorically contended that on the date of accident, when Muruli (hereinafter called the deceased) was proceeding as a pillion rider in a Honda Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LB- 0847 from Mysore road towards Sumanahalli and when he reached near Sri Malai Mahadeshwara Temple, Nagarbhavi, Bangalore, at that time the driver of Mini bus bearing No.KA-11-B-2969 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle, result of which, Muruli fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died at the spot.
11.

In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.1 who is the wife of deceased got examined herself as Pw1 and produced in all 10 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 and Ex.P10 are the police documents i.e., F.I.R with complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, Inquest Mahazar, PM report, IMV report, charge sheet, statement of witnesses (5 in nos), notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV act and reply given thereon etc which are the material documents to prove the present point.

12. On the basis of the complaint lodged by Lokesh F, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0067/2024 of Jnanabharathi Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under sections 279, 304 (A) of IPC.

The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under sections 279,
337, 304-A of IPC.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has seriously disputed the manner of accident one stated by the petitioners and submitted that the deceased who was riding in the motorcycle as pillion rider was under the influence of alcohol and even the rider of motorcycle has also consumed alcohol and the rider of the motorcycle by riding the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner on the middle of the road lost control over the vehicle and at the same time, the deceased who was the pillion rider had also lost control and accidentally fall down from the motorcycle on the road and without anticipating the fall of the deceased on the motorcycle, the offending vehicle which was proceeding on the same direction ran over the deceased.
Hence there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In order to substantiate the said contention, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has referred the averments of the complaint, spot mahazar, Inquest mahazar and the FSL report as at Ex.P1, Ex.P2, Ex.P4 and Ex.R4 respectively .

14. Per contra, the learned counsel for petitioners by referring the evidence of RW.2 and the statement of RW.2 at Ex.P8 has vehemently submitted that the accident in question has occurred not due to the fall of the deceased accidentally, instead the driver of the offending vehicle by driving it in rash and negligent manner in his attempt to over take the vehicle on the left side of the motorcycle touched on the left handle of the motorcycle result of which, the pillion rider fell on the road and the offending vehicle ran over the pillion rider further result of which, the pillion rider succumbed to the injuries.
15. If the police records are perused, RW.2 Raju was the rider of the motorcycle and deceased was the pillion rider in the motorcycle.
The complaint was lodged by the brother of the deceased.

In the complaint, the complainant has clearly stated that the pillion rider i.e., deceased accidentally fall from the motorcycle and the offending vehicle which was coming from the same direction ran over the pillion rider.

Even in the spot mahazar and in the inquest mahazar which were drawn on the next date of the accident very same contention was taken stating that the pillion rider accidentally fall from the motorcycle and the offending vehicle which was proceeding on the same road ran over the body of the deceased.
16. If the evidence of RW.2-Raju who is the rider of the motorcycle is perused, during his examination in chief he has admitted the contents of the complaint as true.

But, during the cross examination by the learned counsel for petitioners, he has given evidence against to the averments of the complaint stating that the offending vehicle touched to the handle of the motorcycle result of which, the deceased fell down and the bus ran over the deceased.
In the statement under Ex.P8, the RW.2 has stated the very same fact.

Having admitted the contents of the complaint as true and correct, when it has turned to the cross examination by the learned counsel for petitioners, the RW.2 has stated that accident was due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle because of the offending vehicle touched to the handle of the motorcycle.
Hence, the evidence of RW.2 cannot be relied upon and he is not a trust worthy witness.
It is further relevant to state here that the statement of RW.2 as per Ex.P8 was stated to have been recorded on 24.02-2024.

If really, RW.2 had given statement as per Ex.P8 on 24.02.2024, then in the inquest mahazar and in the spot mahazar, the investigating officer would not have recorded that the deceased was accidentally fall from the motorcycle.

Hence Ex.P8 given under Section 162 of Cr.P.C. cannot be relied upon and on that basis, it cannot be said that accident was caused due to the touch of the handle of the offending Venkatalakshmi vs Prathima N on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146720145/
5 vehicle to the motorcycle.

If FSL report at Ex.R4 marked through RW.3-the Police Inspector Gnanabharathi Sanchari Police Station is perused, wherein there is clear mention about the consumption of alcohol by the deceased of the quantity of 269.93 mg/100 ml.

17. The learned counsel for petitioners has posed many more questions to the RW.1-the official of Respondent No.1 stating that FLS report was not collected from the scientific investigating office and that it does not bear the seal and signature of the concerned police station, hence it cannot be relied upon.
18.
If Ex.R4 is perused, as observed supra, the said document is produced by the Respondent No.2 through the RW.3.
It is true that RW.3 is not the investigating officer in the accident in question.

But, being the Police Inspector of the Gnanabharathi Sanchari Police Station within which case was registered relating to the present accident, he is competent to produce the document before the court relating to the present case.
Further, Ex.R4 is digitally signed and it is the true copy of the FSL report attested by the Police Inspector of the concerned police station.
Further the FSL report is admissible under Sec.293 of Cr.P.C.
Hence Ex.R4 can very well be relied upon.
From the Ex.R4 it can be gathered that on the date of the accident, the deceased had consumed excess alcohol and under the influence of alcohol he was travelling in the motorcycle as pillion rider.
19. The learned counsel for petitioners has submitted that there is no bar to travel in the motorcycle as pillion rider under the influence of alcohol.
20. It is true that no offence under Sec. 185 of MV Act would attract even if pillion rider travels in the motorcycle under the influence of Alcohol.

But, when it can be gathered from the FSL report that the deceased had consumed excess alcohol and one cannot have control over his body and mind by consuming alcohol of the capacity of 269.93 mg, under such circumstances, there is every reason to believe that the deceased having consumed excess alcohol by not sitting properly in the pillion seat he lost control over his body and mind and accidentally fall from the motorcycle.
21. Further, if the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the deceased was proceeding in the motorcycle as pillion rider from Mysore road towards Sumanahalli.
The offending vehicle was also proceeding on the same direction.
The offending vehicle is a heavy vehicle when compared to the motorcycle as offending vehicle is a bus.
The spot of accident is on the middle of the road.
The RW.2 being the rider of the motorcycle ought to have ride the motorcycle on the left side of the road.

But,
against to the traffic rules, he rode his vehicle on the middle of the road.
Hence, from the topography of the scene of the occurrence it can be said that both the rider, pillion rider and the driver of the offending vehicle have contributed negligence.
The rider of the motorcycle by riding the vehicle on the middle of the road has contributed negligence.
The deceased by traveling in the motorcycle as pillion rider under the influence of excess alcohol fall accidentally from the vehicle has contributed negligence.

So far as the offending vehicle is concerned, if the driver of the offending vehicle had driven his vehicle in moderate speed by maintaining distance between the two vehicles,
on seeing the pillion rider fall on the road he could have applied break and could have avoided the accident to some extent.

Hence the negligence contributed by the rider and pillion rider of the motorcycle is assessed at the ratio of 15% each (ie.,) together 30% and the driver of the offending Venkatalakshmi vs Prathima N on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146720145/
6 vehicle at the ratio of 70%.
22.

It is relevant to state here that the respondent No.2 in their written statement has categorically stated that the petition filed by the petitioners is bad for non- joinder of necessary party for the reason that the petitioners have not arrayed the insurer and insured of the motorcycle.
If the documents placed on record is perused, the wife of the deceased is the RC owner of the motorcycle.

Had the petitioners arrayed the owner and insurer of the motorcycle, they would have get compensation from the insurer of the motorcycle to the extent of negligence contributed by the rider of the motorcycle.

Since the petitioners have not arrayed the owner and insurer of the motorcycle,
the petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 30%.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Partly affirmative.
23. Issue No.2:

It is the contention taken by the petitioners that, petitioner No.1 being the wife and petitioner no.2 and 3 being the minor children and petitioner no.4 and 5 being the parents of the deceased are entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased and that deceased was working as Painter and earning a sum of Rs. 40,000/- p.m.
24.
It is stated that at the time of accident, deceased was aged about 40 years.
The petitioners have produced Aadhaar card of the deceased which reflects the date of the birth of deceased as 05-05- 1983.
As the accident in question has taken place in the year 2024, it can be said that the deceased was aged about 41 years as on the date of accident.
25. So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as observed earlier, as per the case of petitioners, deceased was painter and earning Rs.40,000/- p.m.
In this regard, petitioners have not produced any document.
Hence notional income needs to be considered.

Hence considering the age of petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence, takes the income of the petitioner as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
26.
The petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner no.2 and 3 being the minor children and petitioner no.4 and 5 being the parents of the deceased are the dependents of the deceased.

27. Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife, minor children, parents and they are stated to have resided together with the deceased, 1/4th of the annual income is to be deducted towards he personal expenses and remaining 3/4th is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.

28. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors/Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40% of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the Venkatalakshmi vs Prathima N on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146720145/
7 deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
Hence in the instant case as the victim was 41 years the addition towards future prospect should be 25%.

29. Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/-, by adding 25% towards future prospect it comes to Rs.20,625/-, out of it if 1/4 is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.15,469/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group of 41 to 45 is '14'.

Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.25,98,792/-
(Rs.15,469/- x 14 x 12 =25,98,792/-).
30.

Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 has lost her husband, petitioner no.2 and 3 have lost their father and Petitioner No.4 and 5 have lost their son in their old age, thereby lost the love and affection of deceased.

So far as the quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
It is further observed that the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

31. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lombord Insurance Co. Ltd, the Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lombord Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of filial consortium.

Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and Rs.18,150/- towards loss of estate.
32.

In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
 SL Heads Amount  1 Transportation and Rs. 18,150/-
Funeral
Expenses

2 Loss of estate Rs. 18,150/-
 3. Loss of spousal Rs.2,42,000/-
 consortium, Parental  consortium and Filial  consortium  (Rs.48,400x5)
 4. Loss of Dependency Rs.25,98,792/-
 Total Rs.28,77,092/-

8
Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.28,77,092/- and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
33. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with the 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

34. Since deceased and rider together had contributed negligence to an extent of 30% and respondent No.2 had contributed negligence to an extent of 70% this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 30%.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to pay 70% of the awarded compensation to the petitioners.

70% of the compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
accordingly issue no 2 is answered.
35.
Issue No.3: In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.28,77,092/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakh Seventy Seven Thousand Ninety Two only).

The Respondent no.2 is liable to pay 70% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.20,13,964/- +
cost of Rs.1,000/- imposed vide order on IA No.I & II.

The respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the compensation of Rs.20,14,964/- (Rupees Twenty Lakhs Fourteen Thousand Nine Hundred Sixty Four only) with interest within 2 months from the date of this award.
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum on Rs.20,13,964/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Petitioners shall forgo 30% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.8,63,128/-.
Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.9,14,964/- Petitioner No.2 and 3 are entitled for Rs.3,00,000/- each Petitioner No.4 is entitled for Rs.2,50,000/-
Petitioner No.5 is entitled for Rs.2,50,000/-

Out of the amount, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner on proper identification through E-payment.

So far as the amount apportioned to the petitioners no.4 and 5 are concerned same is ordered to be released in their favour after due identification through E -payment.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has seriously disputed the manner of accident one stated by the petitioners and submitted that the deceased who was riding in the motorcycle as pillion rider was under the influence of alcohol and even the rider of motorcycle has also consumed alcohol and the rider of the motorcycle by riding the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner on the middle of the road lost control over the vehicle and at the same time, the deceased who was the pillion rider had also lost control and accidentally fall down from the motorcycle on the road and without anticipating the fall of the deceased on the motorcycle, the offending vehicle which was proceeding on the same direction ran over the deceased.
Hence there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Had the petitioners arrayed the owner and insurer of the motorcycle, they would have get compensation from the insurer of the motorcycle to the extent of negligence contributed by the rider of the motorcycle.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But, being the Police Inspector of the Gnanabharathi Sanchari Police Station within which case was registered relating to the present accident, he is competent to produce the document before the court relating to the present case.
Further the FSL report is admissible under Sec.293 of Cr.P.C.
From the Ex.R4 it can be gathered that on the date of the accident, the deceased had consumed excess alcohol and under the influence of alcohol he was travelling in the motorcycle as pillion rider.
20. It is true that no offence under Sec. 185 of MV Act would attract even if pillion rider travels in the motorcycle under the influence of Alcohol.
But, when it can be gathered from the FSL report that the deceased had consumed excess alcohol and one cannot have control over his body and mind by consuming alcohol of the capacity of 269.93 mg, under such circumstances, there is every reason to believe that the deceased having consumed excess alcohol by not sitting properly in the pillion seat he lost control over his body and mind and accidentally fall from the motorcycle.
The offending vehicle is a heavy vehicle when compared to the motorcycle as offending vehicle is a bus.
The spot of accident is on the middle of the road.
The RW.2 being the rider of the motorcycle ought to have ride the motorcycle on the left side of the road.
But,
against to the traffic rules, he rode his vehicle on the middle of the road.
Hence, from the topography of the scene of the occurrence it can be said that both the rider, pillion rider and the driver of the offending vehicle have contributed negligence.
The rider of the motorcycle by riding the vehicle on the middle of the road has contributed negligence.
The deceased by traveling in the motorcycle as pillion rider under the influence of excess alcohol fall accidentally from the vehicle has contributed negligence.
So far as the offending vehicle is concerned, if the driver of the offending vehicle had driven his vehicle in moderate speed by maintaining distance between the two vehicles,
on seeing the pillion rider fall on the road he could have applied break and could have avoided the accident to some extent.
Hence the negligence contributed by the rider and pillion rider of the motorcycle is assessed at the ratio of 15% each (ie.,) together 30% and the driver of the offending Venkatalakshmi vs Prathima N on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146720145/
6 vehicle at the ratio of 70%.
22.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

The petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.28,77,092/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakh Seventy Seven Thousand Ninety Two only).

cost of Rs.1,000/- imposed vide order on IA No.I & II.
The respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the compensation of Rs.20,14,964/- (Rupees Twenty Lakhs Fourteen Thousand Nine Hundred Sixty Four only) with interest within 2 months from the date of this award.
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum on Rs.20,13,964/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Petitioners shall forgo 30% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.8,63,128/-.

Petitioner No.5 is entitled for Rs.2,50,000/-
Out of the amount, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner on proper identification through E-payment.
Entire compensation amount is ordered to be deposited in the names of minor petitioner no.2 and petitioner No.3 till they attains the age of majority reserving right to the petitioner no.1 to withdrawn the accrued interest for the maintenance and welfare of the minor.

Draw award accordingly.
